accepted.s: In the revised estimates for 2025-26, which source constituted the largest share of Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue?
accepted.x: Mines and Minerals was the largest source of Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue in 2025-26 RE, accounting for 37 per cent.
accepted.tq: Use the largest-source comparison and distinguish it from the next-largest head.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: The own non-tax revenue of Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26 RE was estimated at approximately:
accepted.x: Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue was estimated at ₹14,324 crore in 2025-26 RE, compared with ₹5,972 crore earlier.
accepted.tq: Compare the stated estimates and select the exact aggregate figure.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the composition of Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue in 2025-26 RE?
o: Mines and Minerals was followed by Medical and Health.
Interest Receipts constituted the second-largest source after Mines and Minerals.
Police receipts exceeded Medical and Health receipts.
Forests was the largest source, followed by Education.
accepted.x: In 2025-26 RE, Mines and Minerals accounted for 37 per cent and Medical and Health for 34 per cent, making them the first and second-largest sources respectively.
accepted.tq: Apply the ranking in the latest composition rather than relying only on individual amounts.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding own non-tax revenue of Andhra Pradesh:
1. Interest receipts are a component of non-tax revenue.
2. Royalties and user charges are included in non-tax revenue.
3. Non-tax revenue is raised exclusively through taxes on the public.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Interest receipts, royalties and user charges are forms of non-tax revenue. Statement 3 is false because non-tax revenue consists of receipts not raised by taxing the public.
accepted.tq: Find the statement that reverses the definition of non-tax revenue.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II with reference to selected heads of Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue in 2024-25 RE:
List-I (Head)
 a. Mines and Minerals
 b. Police
 c. Medical and Health
 d. Education
List-II (Amount in ₹ crore)
 i. 55
 ii. 313

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: In 2024-25 RE, Mines and Minerals was ₹3,518 crore, Police ₹389 crore, Medical and Health ₹313 crore and Education ₹55 crore.

accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly represents the trend in the share of Mines and Minerals in Andhra Pradesh's own non-tax revenue?
o: 50 per cent in 2023-24 and 41 per cent in 2024-25 RE
34 per cent in 2023-24 and 37 per cent in 2024-25 RE
37 per cent in 2023-24 and 34 per cent in 2024-25 RE
41 per cent in 2023-24 and 50 per cent in 2024-25 RE
accepted.x: The share of Mines and Minerals increased from 41 per cent in 2023-24 to 50 per cent in 2024-25 RE.
accepted.tq: Check the direction of change before selecting the percentage pair.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: In the revised estimates for 2024-25, which sequence correctly ranks the major components of Andhra Pradesh's revenue receipts from highest to lowest share?
o: Own Tax, Central Transfers, Own Non-Tax
Own Non-Tax, Own Tax, Central Transfers
Central Transfers, Own Tax, Own Non-Tax
Own Tax, Own Non-Tax, Central Transfers
accepted.x: The ranking in 2024-25 RE was Own Tax, Central Transfers and Own Non-Tax. Own Non-Tax was the smallest of the three components.
accepted.tq: Arrange the components by relative share rather than by absolute revenue alone.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Andhra Pradesh's own revenue in 2024-25 is correct?
o: Own non-tax revenue exceeded its budget estimate.
Central transfers formed the smallest component of revenue receipts.
Own non-tax revenue fell from the budget estimate of ₹10,576 crore to the revised estimate of ₹7,018 crore.
Own tax revenue was lower than own non-tax revenue.
accepted.x: Own non-tax revenue was revised downward from the budget estimate of ₹10,576 crore to ₹7,018 crore.
accepted.tq: Test the direction of revision and reject reversed budget-revised figures.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: Before the introduction of GST, which item accounted for approximately 73 per cent of Andhra Pradesh's total tax revenue in 2016-17 RE?
accepted.x: Before GST, Sales Tax/VAT accounted for approximately 73 per cent of Andhra Pradesh's total tax revenue in 2016-17 RE.
accepted.tq: Use the pre-GST and post-GST distinction to identify the relevant tax source.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s:
With reference to the post-GST tax structure in Andhra Pradesh, consider the following statements:
1. SGST accounted for about 40 per cent in 2025-26 RE.
2. Sales tax continues mainly on petroleum products and liquor.
3. Sales tax was completely abolished for every commodity after GST.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: SGST accounted for about 40 per cent in 2025-26 RE, while sales tax continues mainly on petroleum products and liquor. Statement 3 is false because these items remain outside GST.
accepted.tq: Identify the exception to the general post-GST position.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: The Goods and Services Tax in India was introduced on 1 July 2017 under which Constitutional Amendment Act?
accepted.x: GST commenced on 1 July 2017 under the 101st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2016.
accepted.tq: Match the implementation date with the correct constitutional amendment.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s:
Match the following constitutional provisions with their GST-related subjects:
List-I (Article)
 a. Article 246A
 b. Article 269A
 c. Article 279A
List-II (Subject)
 i. GST Council
 ii. Levy and collection of IGST in the course of inter-State trade
 iii. Concurrent power to make laws relating to GST
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Article 246A provides concurrent GST legislative power, Article 269A concerns IGST, and Article 279A establishes the GST Council.
accepted.tq: Start with the familiar GST Council provision and eliminate mismatched articles.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: In the GST Council, the voting weight is divided between the Centre and the States in which manner?
accepted.x: The Centre has one-third of the voting weight and all the States together have two-thirds.
accepted.tq: Distinguish voting weight from the separate majority required for decisions.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: Across all States during 2014-15 to 2023-24, own tax revenue constituted approximately what share of revenue receipts?
accepted.x: Own tax revenue formed approximately 47 per cent of revenue receipts across all States during the stated period.
accepted.tq: Select the stated approximate share without confusing it with Andhra Pradesh's individual-year share.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a usual component of non-tax revenue?
o: Dividends and profits of public sector undertakings
Compulsory tax collected from the public
accepted.x: Non-tax revenue includes dividends, profits, fees, fines, penalties, user charges, royalties and departmental receipts. A compulsory tax is tax revenue, not non-tax revenue.
accepted.tq: Find the option that contradicts the definition of non-tax revenue.
accepted.sec: AP own non-tax revenue - largest source

accepted.s: In February 2021, Andhra Pradesh became eligible for additional borrowing after completing power-sector reforms prescribed by which authority?
o: Department of Expenditure, Ministry of Finance
accepted.x: The power-sector reforms were prescribed by the Department of Expenditure under the Ministry of Finance and were linked to eligibility for additional borrowing.
accepted.tq: Identify the authority connected with reform-linked borrowing permission.
accepted.sec: Reform-linked additional borrowing - reforms and AP's order

accepted.s: For 2026-27, interest payments of Andhra Pradesh were estimated at ₹37,281 crore. This represented approximately what share of revenue receipts?
accepted.x: Interest payments of ₹37,281 crore were estimated to account for 16 per cent of revenue receipts in 2026-27.
accepted.tq: Link the absolute amount with its stated percentage share.

accepted.s: For 2026-27, the pension expenditure of Andhra Pradesh was estimated at:
accepted.x: Pension expenditure was estimated at ₹23,713 crore in 2026-27, equivalent to about 10 per cent of revenue receipts.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the pension figure from the larger interest-payment figure.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly reflects the movement in Andhra Pradesh's interest payments?
o: ₹32,944 crore in 2023-24 and ₹29,481 crore in 2024-25 RE
₹29,481 crore in 2024-25 RE and ₹32,944 crore in 2025-26 RE
₹29,481 crore in 2023-24 and ₹32,944 crore in 2024-25 RE
₹37,233 crore in 2023-24 and ₹29,481 crore in 2024-25 RE
accepted.x: Interest paid increased from ₹29,481 crore in 2023-24 to ₹32,944 crore in 2024-25 RE.
accepted.tq: Check both the year and the direction of change in the paired figures.
accepted.sec: Committed expenditure - salaries, pensions, interest

accepted.s: Interest payments of Andhra Pradesh rose from ₹32,967 crore in 2024-25 to ₹37,233 crore in 2025-26 RE. The increase was:
accepted.x: The increase was ₹37,233 crore minus ₹32,967 crore, equal to ₹4,266 crore.
accepted.tq: Subtract the earlier year's expenditure from the revised estimate.
accepted.sec: Committed expenditure - salaries, pensions, interest

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Andhra Pradesh's fiscal position:
1. The State continued to run a primary deficit.
2. Interest payments and principal repayment together accounted for 18 paise of every rupee in 2026-27.
3. Interest payments and principal repayment were lower than welfare expenditure in the same comparison.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The State continued to run a primary deficit, and interest plus principal repayment accounted for 18 paise of every rupee. Statement 3 is false because this was described as level with welfare expenditure, which accounted for 17 paise.
accepted.tq: Compare the stated expenditure shares and reject the reversed comparison.
accepted.sec: Committed expenditure - salaries, pensions, interest

accepted.s: According to the reported CAG monthly data, revenue expenditure of Andhra Pradesh crossed what proportion of its annual estimate by November in each of the last three years?
accepted.x: Revenue expenditure crossed 60 per cent of the annual estimate by November in each of the last three years.
accepted.tq: Identify the precise threshold rather than selecting a nearby rounded figure.
accepted.sec: Committed expenditure - salaries, pensions, interest

accepted.s: In 2023-24, committed expenditure together with subsidies accounted for what share of revenue expenditure across all States?
accepted.x: Committed expenditure plus subsidies accounted for 51.76 per cent of revenue expenditure across all States in 2023-24.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the combined share from the individual expenditure components.
accepted.sec: Committed expenditure - salaries, pensions, interest

accepted.s: High interest payments, administrative costs and welfare commitments are associated with which of the following consequences in Andhra Pradesh's finances?
o: Fiscal rigidity and crowding out of capital outlay
Automatic elimination of the revenue deficit
Complete replacement of revenue expenditure by capital expenditure
accepted.x: High interest payments, administrative costs and welfare commitments create fiscal rigidity and crowd out capital outlay.
accepted.tq: Trace the stated cause-effect relationship from committed costs to capital expenditure.
accepted.sec: Committed expenditure - salaries, pensions, interest
